newsitem.title: USA: Weather satellite set for launch from Florida.
newsitem.headline: Weather satellite set for launch from Florida.

text.p: The U.S. space agency said it would try to launch a $220 million weather satellite early on Thursday, weather permitting.

The GOES-K satellite, riding atop an Atlas rocket, was set to blastoff from Cape Canaveral at 1:50 a.m. EST (0550 GMT) on Thursday, but forecasters said there was only a one-in-ten chance of an on-time launch because of stormy weather.
The forecast for Friday looked much better, launch weather officer Joel Tumbiolo said.
The new satellite will back up two existing GOES spacecraft, watching both coasts of North America from a stationary orbit 22,300 miles (35,890 km) above the equator.
The GOES 8 and 9 satellites have experienced technical problems, so forecasters are eager to have a new satellite standing by in case of a failure.
"The comfort of having the back up is what we need now," Susan Zevin, deputy director for operations at the National Weather Service, said.

Weather forecasters rely on the satellites to give warnings of thunderstorms, winter storms, flash floods and other severe weather. The GOES network also provides early detection and tracking of hurricanes.
